meta.triageRationale: One cohesive story with a real design choice and several build tasks. The queue (src/daemon/queue.ts IndexQueue) is shared by code jobs and LLM-backed summary jobs with one worker, and a whole-repo summary sweep is a single job, so splitting needs a decision on the concurrency model (two concurrent workers vs one worker that serves the code lane first and lets a sweep yield between entities), on which job kinds go to which lane (config and reembed jobs), and on how status is reported. It touches the queue, the daemon wiring that starts/stops it and reports depth (src/daemon/index.ts: start :289, freshness :821, status :1060, compaction guard :1635, stop :2039), repo.stats (src/daemon/repo-stats.ts:163), the indexer's enqueuers and dispatcher (src/indexer/index.ts :402-403, :759, :818) and the code-review freshness reader (src/workflow/code-review/freshness.ts). Two modules (daemon, indexer), no storage schema change. Grounding is from direct search of every queue user (the request's sizing question is which call sites use the queue, which a grep answers completely), not from an analyze bundle.

summary.prose: The daemon's index queue gets two lanes that run at the same time: an index lane for code and file work, and a summary lane for document summaries. Code indexing no longer waits behind a summary sweep that can take hours. In the summary lane, a document that was just edited is summarised before the rest of a sweep, and a running sweep stops between documents to do it. A summary is stored only if its document still exists with the text that was summarised. Status shows each lane's depth and whether it is running.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Run document summarisation on its own queue so code indexing never waits on it

api.name: IndexQueue.enqueue
postconditions: doc-summarise-repo and doc-summarise-entity jobs go to the summary lane; every other kind goes to the index lane.
Each kind keeps today's dedup, applied within its lane.
A doc-summarise-entity job is placed ahead of the first doc-summarise-repo job queued in the summary lane, after any other queued doc-summarise-entity jobs.
The enqueue wakes only the lane it went to.

api.name: IndexQueue.start

returns.meaning: Resolves when both lanes have stopped.

postconditions: Each lane runs its own drain loop, and the two run at the same time; within a lane jobs run one at a time, in order.
A job that throws is logged as today (including the store-lock case) and its lane continues.

api.name: IndexQueue.takeDocSummaryEdit

returns.meaning: The first queued doc-summarise-entity job, removed from the summary lane, or undefined.

postconditions: A job it returns is no longer queued and is not counted by depth.

api.name: IndexQueue.laneStatus
api.signature: laneStatus(): { index: { depth: number; running: boolean }; summary: { depth: number; running: boolean } }

returns.meaning: Each lane's queued count and whether its worker is running a job.

api.name: IndexQueue state readers
api.signature: depth: number; isProcessing: boolean; isStopping: boolean; depthForRepo(repoPath: string): number; codeIndexWorkFor(repoPath: string): { inFlight: boolean; pending: number }; stop(): void

returns.meaning: depth and depthForRepo count both lanes; isProcessing is true while either lane runs a job; codeIndexWorkFor reads the index lane only (its in-flight job and queue); stop ends both lanes after their current jobs. isStopping is true once stop() has been called; the sweep reads it as shouldStop.

postconditions: daemon.compact, repo.stats, codeReview.freshness and shutdown keep their current calls and meaning.
depthForRepo counts a doc-summarise-repo job queued in the summary lane, and never a doc-summarise-entity job, as today.

api.name: runDocSummarySweep
api.signature: runDocSummarySweep(entityIds: readonly string[], deps: { getEntity(id: string): Promise<Entity | null>; summarise(entity: Entity): Promise<SummariseDocResult>; takeEdit(): { entityId: string } | undefined; runEdit(entityId: string): Promise<void>; shouldStop(): boolean; onProgress(done: number, total: number): void }): Promise<{ summarised: number; skipped: number; failed: number; gone: number; stopped: boolean }>

parameters.name: entityIds
parameters.purpose: The repo's document and section entity ids, listed at the start of the sweep.

postconditions: Before each entity it checks shouldStop(); when true it returns at once with stopped: true, so stop() ends a sweep after the summary in progress.
Before each entity, every queued single-document job is taken and run first (each also after a shouldStop() check).
Each entity is re-read just before it is summarised; one that no longer exists is counted as gone and skipped.
A throw for one entity is counted as failed and the sweep continues, as today.
onProgress is called after each entity with the number done and the total.

Results are classified as: ok:true and skipped 'unchanged' -> skipped; ok:true otherwise -> summarised; skipped 'entity-gone' or 'body-changed' (or the entity missing on re-read) -> gone; ok:false with another skipped reason ('not-a-doc', 'body-empty') -> skipped; ok:false with an error -> failed; a throw -> failed.

api.name: buildDaemonStatus / DaemonStatus
api.signature: DaemonStatusSources.queueLanes?: () => QueueLanes; DaemonStatus.queueLanes?: QueueLanes, where QueueLanes = { index: { depth: number; running: boolean }; summary: { depth: number; running: boolean; sweep?: { repoPath: string; done: number; total: number } } }

returns.meaning: queueDepth stays the total of both lanes; queueLanes is added.

postconditions: A consumer that does not know queueLanes sees no change.
The daemon builds queueLanes from queue.laneStatus() and IndexerService.summarySweepProgress().
buildDaemonStatus copies it; when the source is absent the field is absent.

api.name: writeDocSummaryIfCurrent
api.signature: writeDocSummaryIfCurrent(db: DbClient, entityId: string, repo: string, summary: DocSummary): Promise<"written" | "entity-gone" | "body-changed">

parameters.name: summary
parameters.purpose: Carries contentHash, the sha256 of the body that was summarised.

returns.meaning: Whether the row was written, and why not.

errors.code: Error: writeDocSummary: repo is not registered
errors.when: The repo is not registered (the same throw as writeDocSummary).
The write transaction fails (thrown as from writeDocSummary).

postconditions: Inside one write transaction: when the entity row is absent, or its u64 is unknown, nothing is written and 'entity-gone' is returned; when sha256 of the stored row's body differs from summary.contentHash nothing is written and 'body-changed' is returned; otherwise the row is written exactly as writeDocSummary writes it and 'written' is returned.
writeDocSummary itself and its callers are unchanged.

api.name: summariseDoc

returns.meaning: SummariseDocResult.skipped gains 'entity-gone' and 'body-changed'; a summary the conditional write did not store is { ok: false, skipped: 'entity-gone' | 'body-changed' }.

postconditions: Both writes (the summary and the error placeholder) go through writeDocSummaryIfCurrent.
Summary write: a throw is reported as persistence-failed, as today; 'entity-gone' or 'body-changed' is reported as { ok: false, skipped: <reason> }.

Placeholder write: a throw keeps today's behaviour (logged; the result carries the original model error); 'entity-gone' or 'body-changed' takes precedence over the model error and is reported as { ok: false, skipped: <reason> }, since the failed document is no longer current.

api.name: IndexerService.summarySweepProgress
api.signature: summarySweepProgress(): { repoPath: string; done: number; total: number } | undefined

returns.type: { repoPath: string; done: number; total: number } | undefined
returns.meaning: The running sweep's progress, or undefined when no sweep runs.

postconditions: IndexerService owns the progress: docSummariseRepo sets it before runDocSummarySweep, updates it from onProgress, and clears it in a finally block, so it is cleared when the sweep completes, stops or throws.

dataModelChanges.details: The queue holds two lanes, each with its own in-flight job. No stored data changes; the in-memory queue is still lost on restart, as today.
Optional queueLanes (per-lane depth, running, and the running sweep's progress). Additive; queueDepth unchanged.

A summary row written by the summariser is written only for an entity that exists with the summarised body, checked in the write transaction by the new writeDocSummaryIfCurrent; writeDocSummary is unchanged for its other callers.

errorCases.scenario: A code job deletes or rewrites a document while the summary lane is summarising it.
errorCases.detection: writeDocSummaryIfCurrent reads the entity row inside its write transaction and compares the body hash.
errorCases.response: Nothing is written ('entity-gone' or 'body-changed'). Re-summarising a rewritten document is best-effort: the file event queues its single-document jobs, but an enqueue failure is only logged (src/indexer/index.ts:812-825); otherwise the next full index's sweep picks it up. A rewrite made by a full index is picked up by that index's own sweep.
errorCases.userImpact: No summary is written for a deleted document or from text that has since changed. A summary already stored still lags its document until that document is summarised again, as today (docs/plans/docs-module.md).

errorCases.scenario: A job throws in either lane.
errorCases.detection: The lane loop catches it, as today.
errorCases.response: Logged (store-lock case named as today); that lane continues; the other lane is unaffected.

errorCases.scenario: Shutdown while a summary is running.
errorCases.detection: stop() sets both lanes to end and isStopping; the sweep checks shouldStop() before each entity.
errorCases.response: Each lane finishes its current job; a running sweep returns after the summary in progress. start resolves when both lanes have ended. Shutdown still has its hard-exit backstop at 20 s (src/daemon/shutdown.ts:117), which exits even if a summary is still running, and does not wait for the queue at all when the store has lost its locks (src/daemon/shutdown.ts:136-137); both are unchanged.
errorCases.userImpact: Shutdown waits at most for one summary, bounded by the 20 s backstop, as before.

errorCases.scenario: Memory or GPU pressure from a summary and code embeddings running together.
errorCases.response: Accepted by the stakeholder; revisit (for example a serial mode) if it is seen.

errorCases.scenario: The repo is unregistered or the write transaction fails while storing a summary.
errorCases.response: summariseDoc reports persistence-failed, as today; the sweep counts it as failed and continues.
errorCases.userImpact: That summary is missing until the next sweep.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test via npx tsx --test (assert/strict), run under Node 22

migration.stateBefore: Per s1: one FIFO with one worker runs every job kind (src/daemon/queue.ts:193, src/daemon/index.ts:289); a whole-repo summary sweep is one job (src/indexer/index.ts:918) and every code job queued after it waits for it.
migration.stateAfter: Two lanes run at the same time; summaries no longer delay code indexing; single-document summaries go ahead of sweeps; summaries are written only for current documents; status shows both lanes.

migrationSteps.action: Split IndexQueue into an index lane and a summary lane with concurrent drain loops, edit priority, takeDocSummaryEdit and laneStatus.
Move the sweep loop into runDocSummarySweep (stop check, take queued edits first, re-read each entity) and call it from docSummariseRepo, which owns the sweep progress.
Add writeDocSummaryIfCurrent and route summariseDoc's two writes through it; writeDocSummary is unchanged.
Report queueLanes in daemon.status; record the serial-LLM exception in CLAUDE.md.
Update and restart the installed daemon.

migration.backwardCompat: No stored data changes. writeDocSummary and its callers are unchanged. DaemonStatus gains one optional field; queueDepth keeps its meaning. The in-memory queue is lost on restart, as today.

alternativesConsidered.name: Two lanes inside IndexQueue, one concurrent worker each
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: IndexQueue keeps its API and routes each job to an index lane or a summary lane; start runs one drain loop per lane concurrently; the summary lane puts single-document jobs before sweeps and lets a running sweep take them between entities.
alternativesConsidered.approach: IndexQueue holds two FIFOs. enqueue routes doc-summarise-repo and doc-summarise-entity to the summary lane and every other kind to the index lane, with today's dedup per kind. start(processor) runs two drain loops at once and resolves when both have stopped; each loop is serial. In the summary lane a doc-summarise-entity job is inserted ahead of the first queued doc-summarise-repo job, and takeDocSummaryEdit() removes and returns the first queued doc-summarise-entity job so a running sweep can run it between entities. depth, isProcessing, depthForRepo span both lanes as today; codeIndexWorkFor reads the index lane only; laneStatus() reports each lane's depth and whether it is running. The sweep re-reads each entity before summarising it, and the summary write happens only if the entity still exists with the body that was summarised, checked inside the write transaction.
pros: Callers keep one queue object and today's totals; code indexing never waits on a summary.
Edited documents are summarised within about one summary of the edit.
cons: A summary and code embedding can call Ollama at the same time (accepted exception).

alternativesConsidered.name: Two separate queue instances
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A second IndexQueue for summaries, created and started by the daemon, with the indexer holding both.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The daemon creates an index queue and a summary queue and passes both to IndexerService; every reader that needs totals (status, compaction, repo.stats) combines the two.
pros: Each queue stays a plain single-worker FIFO.
cons: Every reader of queue state changes, and the routing of kinds lives in the enqueuers instead of one place.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Partial on keeping the queue readers correct: every reader of queue state (status, compaction, repo.stats, freshness) would have to combine two queues, and a missed one misreports.

alternativesConsidered.name: One worker, index lane first, sweep yields
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Two FIFOs, one worker that always serves the index lane first; a sweep yields to index work between entities.
alternativesConsidered.approach: As a1 but serial: the worker takes from the index lane while it has jobs; a sweep checks the index lane between entities.
cons: Code work still waits for the summary in progress; the stakeholder chose concurrent lanes.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Rejected by the stakeholder on 2026-10-17: code work would still wait for the summary in progress, and the stakeholder chose lanes that run at the same time.
